title: Rav Yechezkel (father of Rav Yehuda)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a great man of his generation and a man of good deeds in the time of Shmuel, and he merited two sons who were great among Israel, Rami and Rav Yehuda; and the latter was greater in Torah than his father, as is explicit in Kiddushin 32a: Rav Yechezkel was teaching his son Rami the mishnah "Those to be burned among those to be stoned" — Rav Yehuda his son said to him: "Father! Do not teach it thus." And Shmuel, the teacher of Rav Yehuda, told him that he is not permitted to say so to his father in this language. And they said there, 33a, that Rav Yechezkel was so great that even Mar Shmuel would rise before him, since he was a man of good deeds; and therefore he cautioned Rav Yehuda to rise before his father even though he is greater than him in Torah. And we find in the Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot ch. 9, end of halakhah 2, and Taanit ch. 1, halakhah 3: “R[abbi/Rav] … bar Yechezkel” said, "Father would bless upon the descent of rain: 'May Your name, our King, be magnified, sanctified, blessed and exalted for every single drop that You send down to us.'"
And so it is mentioned in Berakhot 11a: Rav Yechezkel taught: One who acted according to the words of Beit Shammai has acted [validly], etc.

notes.text: Hyman’s abbreviated reporter “א״ר בר יחזקאל” is incomplete. The named Guggenheimer Taanit1:3 text spells out Rav Yehuda bar Yechezkel reporting his father’s rain blessing. The body preserves the shortened supplied form; this note gives the independently observed fuller reading.

Kiddushin 32a directly has Yechezkel teaching Rami, Yehudah correcting his father and Shmuel correcting Yehudah’s form of address. Hyman’s shortened Jerusalem Talmud reporter remains incomplete in the body. The fuller rain-blessing witness is reported in the retained current note, without inserting a guessed name into the supplied text.
